clinician.trajectory_summary: An 87-year-old male with a 50-year history of hypertension, >10 years of type 2 diabetes, coronary heart disease, and prior right lung cancer (lobectomy 16 years ago) presented in November 2020 with anorexia and nausea for half a month. He had chronic renal insufficiency with baseline serum creatinine ~187 μmol/L. On presentation, acute renal function deterioration was documented with serum creatinine 428 μmol/L and urea nitrogen 20.9 mmol/L. Laboratory findings revealed elevated IgG (25.65 g/L), elevated total IgE (453.3 IU/mL), low complement C3 (0.53 g/L), and 24-hour urinary protein 2.38 g. Imaging (CT and ultrasound) showed a right lower ureteral mass with right renal and ureteral hydronephrosis and generalized superficial lymph node enlargement. Urine cytology was negative for malignancy. Cystoscopy and ureteroscopy revealed local bulging and stenosis of the right ureteral orifice. A double-J stent was placed and biopsy was obtained. Ureteral biopsy demonstrated extruded and deformed fibrous tissue with IgG-positive and IgG4-positive plasma cells. Renal biopsy confirmed underlying diabetic nephropathy (mesangial proliferation, diffuse basement membrane thickening, foot process fusion) with abundant IgG4-positive plasma cells in the renal interstitium (IgG4+:IgG ratio 35%) and storiform fibrosis, consistent with IgG4-TIN. Serum IgG4 was significantly elevated at 1890 mg/dL. After double-J stent placement, serum creatinine improved to 279 μmol/L. Methylprednisolone was initiated at 32 mg/day and gradually tapered to 16 mg/day after 5 weeks. At one-year follow-up, methylprednisolone was further reduced to 4 mg/day, serum creatinine stabilized at approximately 200 μmol/L, and serum IgG4 decreased to 59 mg/dL.
